born.why: The code prioritizes survival by avoiding species with a history of harm unless no benefit is recorded, prevents eating unknown fruits whole when hungry by defaulting to tasting, and seeks out foods that have historically reduced hunger.

The code prioritizes starvation survival by eating unconditionally when hunger is critical (>90), uses historical data to safely eat known-good fruits, and only tastes new/ambiguous fruits if hunger is high enough to justify the risk of poisoning, otherwise leaving them alone.

The code prioritizes confirmed poison avoidance (direct history) but relaxes the threshold for starvation survival. It uses trait-based inference cautiously, requiring more negative evidence to reject a fruit than previous code did, and prevents unnecessary tasting when full or when no safe data exists.

The code prioritizes exact species history for safety, uses trait-based inference with a strict poison-avoidance threshold when species is unknown, and dynamically chooses between eating (survival), tasting (learning/low hunger), or carrying (preference) based on current hunger levels to maximize longevity.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding fruits with any recorded poisoning unless starving, uses a simple majority vote for known species safety, and handles new fruits with cautious tasting only when hunger is moderate, preventing unnecessary risk while ensuring caloric intake.

The code improves by quantifying benefit (hunger reduction) rather than just binary harm/safe status, allowing Fagi to distinguish between "poisonous" and "nutritionally useless" fruits, and uses a risk threshold to decide whether to eat known-but-dubious fruits based on her current hunger level.

The code prioritizes the proven safe and effective "blue-round-sweet" fruit by eating it fully, while strictly avoiding any key previously marked as poisonous; for unknown fruits, it only takes a cautious taste if hunger exceeds 60, preventing unnecessary risk from untested species.
